steps.u: PlayerFragment crashes with IllegalStateException when you rotate during buffering (crash report MOB-2291). Fix it and make sure PlayerFragmentTest passes.

steps.r:
PlayerFragmentTest > rotateWhileBuffering_keepsPosition FAILED
    java.lang.IllegalStateException: Fragment PlayerFragment{7f3a} not attached to a context.
        at androidx.fragment.app.Fragment.requireContext(Fragment.java:972)
        at com.tuneshelf.player.PlayerFragment$onBuffering$1.invoke(PlayerFragment.kt:118)
3 tests completed, 1 failed

steps.a: The player and its listener live in the fragment, so after rotation the old fragment's listener and delayed runnable still fire against a detached fragment. The player should outlive the configuration change. I could keep the fragment with setRetainInstance, but that's deprecated and keeps the view-bound handler around; moving the player into a ViewModel is the supported route, so I'll do that and expose buffering as StateFlow.

i.new_string:
private val vm: PlayerViewModel by viewModels()
private val player get() = vm.player

steps.a: The crash is gone: the test no longer throws IllegalStateException. It now fails on the position assertion instead. In Robolectric the FakePlayer the test injects through PlayerFragment.playerFactory is no longer used, because the ViewModel builds a real ExoPlayer, so after recreate the position reads 0. The test's injection point needs to move to a ViewModel factory. I haven't changed that yet; want me to add a ViewModelProvider.Factory with a player factory parameter and update the test?

reference.summary: Moved an Android media player out of a fragment into a ViewModel with a StateFlow for buffering state to stop a crash when the screen rotates during buffering. The crash no longer occurs, but the rotation test still fails because its fake player injection no longer reaches the ViewModel, so the fix is unfinished pending a ViewModel factory.
facts: The crash came from a delayed callback calling requireContext on a detached fragment after rotation
The player was moved into an AndroidViewModel and buffering exposed as StateFlow collected with repeatOnLifecycle
The IllegalStateException is gone but the rotation test still fails on the playback position (expected 42000, got 0)
The test's fake player injection no longer applies; a ViewModel factory is proposed but not done

decisions.choice: Move the player into a ViewModel rather than retaining the fragment
decisions.reason: retained fragments are deprecated and keep the view-bound handler alive
